harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 I created an SSH CA (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca, ed25519), used it to sign the host's ed25519 host key producing /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (10-year validity, principals node1/IP/hostname), configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf to present that certificate, and enabled/started the ssh service (it had been socket-only/inactive with no host keys). Verified with a real SSH client that trusted only the CA public key via an @cert-authority known_hosts entry (no pinned host key): connection passed host verification cleanly ("is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate", "Found CA key"), and failed identically with 'Host key verification failed' when the CA was not trusted (negative control). Then ran the mandatory restart protocol on node1: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (242af11e... -> f4658e31...), and re-verified post-restart that ssh is active, the CA-signed cert file persisted, and a CA-only-trusting client again connects without host-key pinning.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline SSH state on node1 (ssh.service inactive, socket-activated, no host keys yet)
Generated host keys via ssh-keygen -A
Created ed25519 SSH CA at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca
Signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host cert (ssh-keygen -s ... -h) valid for node1, its IP, and hostname
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf with HostCertificate directive
Created /run/sshd, validated config with sshd -t, enabled and started ssh service
Verified with ssh -v client using only @cert-authority trust (no host key pinning) that host verification succeeds
Ran negative control with empty known_hosts to confirm verification fails without CA trust
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health, issued systemctl reboot, polled node1 until reachable
Confirmed boot_id changed after restart
Re-verified post-restart that ssh is active, cert files persisted, and CA-only client trust still connects without pinning

evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca (ed25519) with fingerprint SHA256:51/xQUVY8wx3ucSJPuklj+mUKiC3d1xnU2QpvQDnID4

evidence.requirement: Host key signed by the CA, sshd configured to present it
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s produced ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub signed by the CA; sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf added HostCertificate directive; sshd -t validated and ssh service became active and listening on :22

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA connects without host-key pinning
evidence.summary: ssh -v with only @cert-authority entry in known_hosts shows 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' and 'Found CA key', proceeding to publickey auth (host trust succeeded)

evidence.requirement: Negative control: no pinning and no CA trust fails
evidence.summary: With an empty known_hosts (no CA, no pinned key), ssh reports 'Host key verification failed', proving the earlier success came from CA trust

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 242af11e-49fb-4e07-a001-8016b2349acb, ssh active, and presence of CA/cert/config files before restart

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (stream closed as node went down), node unreachable during reboot, then boot_id changed to f4658e31-7059-4a54-9c4b-a4598f74eeb2 once reachable again, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of SSH host-cert setup and functional verification
evidence.summary: After restart, ssh is active, CA/cert/config files persisted unchanged, and a client trusting only the CA (fresh known_hosts_ca file) again connects and passes host verification via the certificate without any host-key pinning
